questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes a point object in kinematics?
options: An object whose size is negligible compared to the distance it travels
An object that is at rest
questions.explanation: A point object is one whose dimensions can be ignored relative to the distance covered. A car treated as a point during a 100 km road trip is a typical example.

options: Always opposite states an object can be in
Relative — they depend on the chosen frame of reference
Only meaningful for objects with mass
questions.explanation: Whether an object is at rest or in motion depends entirely on the frame of reference. A passenger sitting in a moving train is at rest relative to the train but in motion relative to the ground.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT required to specify the position of a particle in 1D motion?
options: A direction (positive sense of the axis)
questions.explanation: Position in kinematics is purely geometric — you need an origin, a positive direction, and a frame of reference. The particle's mass is irrelevant for describing position.
